data.description:
## Observation
A `cp -R` (or `cp -r`) copy of a linked git worktree is not an isolated copy. It keeps the original's `.git` file (`gitdir: <common>/.git/worktrees/<name>`), so any git command run in the copy resolves to the original repository. `git -C <copy> rev-parse --git-common-dir` returns the shared `.git`.

Reproduced 2026-11-02 in a sandbox: fresh repo with `origin` and `gerrit` remotes, `git worktree add ../wt`, `cp -R ../wt ../wt-copy`, then `git -C ../wt-copy remote remove <r>` for each remote. Afterwards `git remote -v` in the main checkout was empty.

On this host the same construction (a "throwaway" `tracker-copy` of `.tickets-tracker` under `.rebar/scratch/`) did two things on 2026-10-27. It removed both remotes from the shared `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.git/config` (bug `affordable-omphacite-sunfish`). It also landed REBUILD SNAPSHOT commits on the real local `tickets` branch (bug `painted-epidermal-shelduck`).

## Impact
Any recipe that does "work on a copy of the tracker" with a file copy can rewrite shared config, move shared refs, and take shared locks. Nothing warns about this, and the damage shows up later as unrelated-looking failures.

## Open question for the plan
How to guard it: rebar could refuse to operate on (or warn about) a worktree whose path does not match the `gitdir` back-pointer recorded in `<common>/worktrees/<name>/gitdir`. Alternatively, a sanctioned "isolated tracker copy" helper could use `git clone`/`git worktree add` and be documented in `docs/concurrency.md`. Not decided.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A rebar command run inside a file-copied linked worktree of the tracker either refuses with a message naming the copy hazard or operates only on an isolated repository, verified by a test that copies a linked worktree and asserts the shared `.git/config` and branch refs are unchanged.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` documents the hazard and the sanctioned way to make an isolated tracker copy.
data.title: A cp -R copy of a linked worktree is a live handle on the shared repo: git commands in the copy rewrite shared config and refs
